questions.question: A tariff protects home producers by:
options: Taxing imports at the border, raising their shelf price so local products compete more easily — with revenue as a bonus
Limiting the quantity of imports allowed

questions.question: Economists dislike quotas more than tariffs because quotas:
options: Hand valuable import licences to favoured firms and yield the state no revenue

questions.question: DUMPING is:
options: Any export sold at a profit
Selling exports below cost or below the home-market price, often to kill competitors before raising prices

questions.question: Protection is "politically easy and economically expensive" because:
options: Its costs fall only on foreigners
Losses are spread thinly over many consumers while gains concentrate on few visible producers and workers

subtopics.title: The Case for Protection Against the Case for Free Trade

questions.question: The standard rebuttal to the infant-industry argument is that:
options: Infants rarely admit to growing up — protection that never lapses breeds permanent inefficiency

questions.question: The employment argument for protection is weakened because:
options: It saves visible jobs while destroying invisible ones — dearer inputs burden downstream producers, and retaliation kills export jobs
Imports create no competition for jobs

questions.question: Which argument for protection do even free traders generally accept?
options: Permanent tariffs on all consumer goods
Anti-dumping action against predatory pricing from abroad

questions.question: The DESIRABLE MIX of trade policy is:
options: Pure free trade with no exceptions
Broadly open trade plus targeted, temporary, conditional protection with sunset clauses — the scalpel, never the blanket

subtopics.title: Export Promotion, Import Substitution, and South Africa's Path

questions.question: Import substitution industrialises by:
options: Replacing imports with home production behind tariff walls — the inward path

questions.question: The recorded weakness of import substitution is that industries built behind walls:
options: Stay small — capped by the home market — and inefficient, since the wall removes pressure to match world costs

questions.question: Export promotion succeeded in East Asia because:
options: Selling to a ceiling-free world market opened scale economies while global competition forced efficiency

questions.question: South Africa's current trade-policy mix is best described as:
options: Full import substitution behind high walls
Pure free trade with zero tariffs

Officially export-led — with automotive incentives the flagship — plus selective protection in contested sectors like poultry, clothing and steel, throttled mainly by logistics and electricity constraints

subtopics.title: Globalisation, the WTO and the Ladder of Integration

questions.question: The WTO was created:
options: In 1995 by the Uruguay Round, succeeding the GATT of 1947 after eight rounds of tariff cutting
In 1947 as a United Nations agency

questions.question: The most-favoured-nation principle requires that:
options: A trade benefit granted to one partner extends to all members — non-discrimination
Each country favours one chosen nation
Imports be taxed above local goods

questions.question: A standing critique of trade liberalisation is that:
options: Tariffs are higher now than in 1947
Rich countries kept protecting agriculture — the very sector where developing countries hold advantage
The WTO has no dispute system

questions.question: The ladder of integration, in order, is:
options: Economic union, common market, customs union, free trade area
Customs union, free trade area, economic union, common market
Common market, customs union, free trade area, economic union
Free trade area (AfCFTA), customs union (SACU), common market, economic union (the EU with the euro)

subtopics.title: The Tuckshop and the Vendors at the Gate

questions.question: Charging each gate vendor R20 a day to trade corresponds to:
options: A tariff — raising the outsiders' costs so the insider competes more easily

questions.question: The three licensed vendors "suddenly love the rule" because:
options: The licence itself becomes valuable — quotas create privileged insiders who then defend the restriction

questions.question: Free kitchen use for the tuckshop is a subsidy that is:
options: Invisible to learners but real — protection hidden in the school's budget rather than at the gate

questions.question: Protecting the tuckshop is politically attractive because:
options: The saved jobs are visible and grateful while eight hundred learners each lose too little to march — concentrated gains, thin-spread losses

subtopics.title: Raising the Young Shop Without Spoiling It

questions.question: The infant-industry argument is respectable because:
options: A genuinely new producer buying small and dear can reach competitive costs once grown to scale — you cannot learn to swim while drowning

questions.question: "The ladder becomes a hammock" when:
options: Protection removes the pressure to improve, and the shop still calls itself an infant at ten years old

questions.question: Honest infant protection requires:
options: A written expiry date, performance pressure through targets, and shelter for genuine infants only
Protection for the oldest firms first

questions.question: The tuckshop's two futures — selling to its own school forever, or getting good enough to sell to other schools — represent:
options: Import substitution with its home-market ceiling, and export promotion with no ceiling but real competition — and the school van as the logistics that must work

questions.question: The district agreement letting any learner buy from any school's vendors, with no gate fees, is:
options: A free trade area — the AfCFTA at continental scale

questions.question: Adding one common gate fee for OUTSIDERS turns the arrangement into:
options: A customs union — like SACU, the world's oldest, which shares the takings by formula

questions.question: The deal's "real cost" stands at the empty tables because:
options: Squeezed mediocre stands close, and their owners bear concentrated losses while everyone else's lunches improve — losers who deserve real help
The kota stand raises prices fivefold

questions.question: The four-part honest summary of globalisation is:
options: Smaller playgrounds, dearer lunches, no losers, no rules
A rulebook that never changes and never argues
Bigger playgrounds, better and cheaper lunches, real losers deserving real help, and a rulebook forever arguing with itself
